brief: Multiple Goldman desks argue the AI buildout's limiting factor is shifting from demand to financing. Goldman forecasts hyperscalers will spend about $1.2 trillion in capex next year against $1.1 trillion of operating cash flow, with 35% debt funded, over $400 billion of issuance. That debt competes with Treasuries for duration buyers: the swaps desk says the USD 10y10y forward rate's 47bp rise between September 22 and October 7 reflected term premium, not Fed expectations, while the 2-year moved 0bp. Credit has lost its usual cushion: IG spreads cover under 15% of all-in yield versus a 2019-2021 average of 45%, CCC spreads sit near 1,250bp, and Broadcom and Oracle CDS hit record levels. Equities show the weakest breadth since the dotcom bubble even as the S&P sits near its high, and semis and memory names are falling despite strong prints like ASML's, because credit uncertainty is delaying infrastructure deals. The Fed hiked 25bp partly on AI-driven inflation Goldman says is about half mismeasurement. A counter-case cites light positioning and reopening buybacks, but Goldman notes a positioning squeeze would not fix the capex-cash-flow gap.
